selection_rationale: XGBoost, with monotonic constraints on Max Heart Rate Achieved, ST Depression (Oldpeak), Major Vessels Colored by Fluoroscopy, Exercise-Induced Angina (directions measured from training-data correlations, not assumed), was preferred as the production model. Its CV rank-score (0.8502) is within 0.03 of the top performer (Logistic Regression, 0.8623), and its recall (0.778) is at least as good as the strongest alternative tree-based model, Random Forest (0.787). Unlike Random Forest — which, even after removing 7 rows of almost-certainly-placeholder missing-data codes (ca=4, thal=0), still showed small non-monotonic wiggles when we swept oldpeak and max heart rate across their range — XGBoost's constraints make that class of artifact structurally impossible, not just less likely, while keeping the same fast, exact SHAP explanations every tree-based model here gets.

feature_labels.slope: Slope of Peak Exercise ST Segment

intended_use: Educational / research decision-support demo only. Not a certified medical device and must not be used for actual clinical diagnosis.
